platform_notes: All Valor terminals run Valor PayTech's own payment application and are managed from the Valor Portal by EPI (endpoint identifier); settings changed in the portal reach a terminal only after a Package Download (Favorites > 6 on keypad models, Menu > Updates on the Android models). Valor's documents split the range into the keypad/Favorites-menu models (VL100, VL100 Pro, VL110, VP100, and by its own QRG the VP550C and standalone VL300) and the Android Main-Menu models (VL500/VL550, VP550/VP550E, VP350, VP800); the RCKT reader and the Virtual Terminal are driven from the ValorPay phone app and the portal. Valor's knowledge base says 'VL100' and 'VL500' throughout; we map VL100 to the VL100 Pro and the 'VL500 / VL550 / VP500 / VP550 / VP550E' articles to the VL550 and VP550E, and the 509-row Device Error Codes table is labelled VL100/VL110 (11 rows VL100/VL300).

entries.title: VL100/VL110/VP100: put the terminal in remote diagnostics mode for support
steps: Press the Favorites button.
Choose 9, Start RD.
Support can then connect to the terminal from their portal.
entries.quote: VL100/VL110/VP100 = Favorites button, followed by 9.Start RD.

entries.title: Valor Connect is not available on the terminal
steps: Valor Connect has to be switched to Yes in the terminal's parameters in the portal (Device Management, Edit Parameters, Terminal & Transaction). Tech support does this.
A package download is then required on the terminal to confirm the change.
On VL100/VL110/VP100: Favorites (star), 6 Package Download, OK.
entries.quote: A Package Download will be required on the Terminal to confirm changes.

entries.title: How long a refund takes to reach the customer
steps: Valor says this is determined by the cardholder's bank.
entries.quote: This is determined by the Card holder’s bank account.

entries.title: VL100/VL110/VP100: reprint a transaction receipt
steps: Press the Favorites button.
Choose 1, Reprint Receipt.
entries.quote: VL100 / VL110 / VP100 = Favorites Button, 1. Reprint Receipt

entries.title: VL100/VL110/VP100: view a previous batch
steps: Press the Menu button and choose Reports.
Choose Closed Summary or Detailed Report.
Select the batch you want.
entries.quote: VL100 / VL110 / VP100 = Menu Button, Reports, Closed Summary or Detailed Report, Select Referenced Batch

entries.title: View a previous batch in the online portal
steps: In the portal, choose Reports in the sidebar menu.
Open the Batch Report.
Enter the EPI in the search field and select the date range of the batch.
entries.quote: enter EPI in the Search field while selecting the Date range of the Batch Report.

entries.title: Battery is inconsistent (VL110 / VL500 series)
steps: Let the battery run down to 0% until the terminal powers itself off.
Charge it overnight.
Use the charging cable and wall adapter that came with the terminal.
entries.quote: Discharge the battery and let it charge overnight. Ensure you are using the provided charging cable and wall adapter to ensure the best use case.
entries.note: The FAQ names the VL110 and VL500.

entries.title: VL100/VL110/VP100: make the terminal pick up changed settings (package download)
steps: Press the Favorites button.
Choose 6, Package Download.
Press OK.
entries.quote: VL100 / VL110 / VP100 = Favorites Button, 6. Package Download, OK

entries.title: Update a VL300 or VP300 PIN pad to the latest app version
steps: Make sure the PIN pad is connected properly to the VL100 / VP100.
Run a Package Download on the terminal.
If the PIN pad does not update, App Download must be switched to Enabled for the terminal in the portal. Ask tech support to enable it.
entries.quote: Ensure the device is connected appropriately to the VL100 / VP100 and perform a Package Download to ensure the latest software is installed.

entries.title: Which connection types each Valor terminal supports
steps: VL100 / VP100: Ethernet and Wi-Fi.
VL110 / VL500: cellular and Wi-Fi.
RCKT: Bluetooth to a mobile phone.
entries.quote: RCKT = Bluetooth to Mobile Phone

entries.title: VL110: turn on the SIM (cellular) connection
steps: Press the Favorites button.
Choose 7, Comm Config.
Choose 2, Comm Config.
Choose GPRS, then Connect.
entries.quote: VL110 = Favorites Button, 7. Comm Config, 2. Comm Config, GPRS, Connect.

entries.title: VL500 series: make the terminal use the SIM (cellular) connection
steps: Press the Menu button and choose Settings.
Choose WIFI Config.
Toggle Wi-Fi off.
entries.quote: VL500 = Menu Button, Settings, WIFI Config, toggle WIFI Off.
entries.note: The FAQ says VL500.

entries.title: Get a merchant receipt by email for each transaction
steps: In the portal, go to My Setting, then Email Setting.
In the drop-down under "Merchant copy via email", select SEND.
Save.
entries.quote: select SEND in the drop-down box below Merchant copy via email followed by Saving.

entries.title: Terminal is not offering paper receipts
steps: Paper Receipt has to be set to Yes in the terminal's parameters in the portal (Device Management, the EPI, Edit Parameters, Receipt section).
Ask tech support to change it.
Then run a Package Download on the terminal.
entries.quote: In the receipt section, select Yes on Paper Receipt. Save and perform a Package Download on the Terminal.

entries.title: Offer both paper and SMS receipts
steps: Both Paper Receipt and SMS Receipt have to be set to Yes in the terminal's parameters in the portal (Edit Parameters, Receipt section).
Ask tech support to change it.
Then run a Package Download on the terminal.
entries.quote: select Yes on Paper Receipt as well as Yes on SMS Receipt. Save and perform a Package Download on the Terminal.

entries.title: Receipt prints noticeably light
steps: Make sure the receipt tray is clean and closed properly.
On a VL110, make sure the terminal is not in Power Save mode.
On battery terminals (VL110 / VL500), make sure the battery is at 45% or more.
entries.quote: Ensure that the receipt tray is clean and closed appropriately, ensure the Terminal is not in Power Save mode (VL110 only) and has at least 45% battery life. (VL110 / VL500)

entries.title: ValorPay mobile app: batch out
steps: Select the Menu button, then Batch.
Select the Menu button again, then Batch Out.
Select Submit.
entries.quote: Select the Menu Button followed by Batch followed by selecting the Menu button again then Batch Out. To complete select Submit.

entries.title: ValorPay mobile app: switch between stores
steps: Tap the merchant name at the top of the screen.
A drop-down lists all your stores. Pick the one you want.
entries.quote: Yes, tap on the Merchant Name on the top of the screen; then a drop down will appear with all the individual Stores listed.

entries.title: Key in a card by hand (manual entry)
steps: At the Present Card screen, start entering the card details on the keypad.
entries.quote: At the Present Card screen start entering the Card Details on the Keypad.

entries.title: Transaction not Permitted (when keying a card in by hand)
steps: Manual entry is not enabled for the terminal.
It has to be enabled for both credit and debit by the provider. Contact tech support.
entries.quote: If it will not allow or says Transaction not Permitted reach out to your ISO for enabling Manual Entry for both Credit and Debit.

entries.title: See why a transaction was declined
steps: Open the Transactions tab in the online portal.
Hover over the decline icon on the transaction. The reason is shown.
entries.quote: Within the Transactions tab in the Online Portal, if you hover over the Decline Icon it will post the reason.

entries.title: Invalid Parameter (during a download)
steps: Close the terminal's batch from the online portal.
Then try the download again.
entries.quote: Close the Terminal’s batch via the Online Portal, then reattempt the Download.
entries.note: The FAQ entry is titled "My VL500 communicates Invalid Parameter."

entries.title: Close a batch from the online portal
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Find the most recent transaction from this EPI.
Select the vertical ellipsis (three dots), then Open Batch.
Select the Action button, then Close Batch.
entries.quote: Then select the Action Button followed by Close Batch.

entries.title: Switch the terminal between auto-batch and manual batch
steps: This is set in the terminal's parameters in the portal: Device Management, the EPI, Edit Parameters, Terminal & Transaction section.
Batch Out is set to Auto with a Settlement Time, or to Manual.
Ask tech support to change it.
entries.quote: In the Terminal & Transaction section, then toggle Batch Out to Auto followed by setting the Settlement Time.

entries.title: Stop the tip report printing at settlement
steps: This is the "Settlement Report Tip (Print)" setting in the Receipt section of the terminal's parameters in the portal. It is set to No.
Ask tech support to change it.
entries.quote: In the Receipt section toggle Settlement Report Tip (Print) to No.

entries.title: Type lowercase letters or special characters in the Wi-Fi password
steps: Press the matching number or character key several times until the character you want appears.
For a lowercase a, press the 2 key 5 times.
For a % sign, press the # key 5 times.
entries.quote: For example, to achieve a lowercase a, press the number 2 button on the keypad 5 times. To achieve a % sign, press the # button on the keypad 5 times.
entries.note: Applies to terminals with a physical keypad.

entries.title: Paper roll size for Valor terminals
steps: Valor terminals accept 2¼ inch by 55 foot thermal paper rolls.
entries.quote: Our Terminals will accept 2¼" by 55' Thermal Paper rolls.
entries.note: Our VL550 sheet gives the printer as 57 mm x 40 mm and the VP800 as 58 mm wide; 2¼ inch is 57 mm.

entries.title: Receipt disclaimer: up to 4 lines
steps: The receipt disclaimer is edited in the terminal's parameters in the portal (Receipt section) and holds up to 4 lines.
A new line is added with Shift + Enter.
Ask tech support to change it.
entries.quote: If there are less than 4 lines, you can add a new line by pressing the Shift key and the Enter key at the same time.

entries.title: Home screen shows options that do not apply to the business
steps: This comes from Tax ID or Fiscal DB information saved against the device in the portal.
Tech support removes it in Merchant Management, saves the terminal and the merchant, and checks Edit Parameters.
entries.quote: Navigate to the 3. Devices page and remove the Tax ID information or the Fiscal DB information.

entries.title: What time recurring payments are charged
steps: Recurring billing runs at 10:00am EST.
entries.quote: Recurring Billing instances are set to process at 10:00am EST.

entries.title: Wi-Fi security types Valor terminals support
steps: Valor devices support WEP, WPA1 and WPA2-PSK password encryption.
entries.quote: Currently Valor devices support WEP, WPA1, WPA2-PSK password encryptions.

entries.title: Size of the merchant logo on the terminal
steps: The logo needs to be 150 x 150 pixels.
A transparent background is preferred.
entries.quote: The logo would need to be 150 x 150 pixels. A transparent background is preferred.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: BIN-based surcharge is supported, dual pricing was not (per FAQ)
steps: The FAQ says the Virtual Terminal supports only BIN-based surcharge, with dual pricing "coming soon".
entries.quote: Currently, we only support BIN-Based Surcharge via the Virtual Terminal.
entries.note: Valor's later Mobile Application User Guide (06/2025) says dual pricing can be enabled for Virtual Terminal transactions, so this FAQ answer may be out of date.

entries.title: Dual pricing: what "Entered Amount" means
steps: It decides how the amount you key in is treated on the dual pricing home screen.
Set to Cash, the keyed amount is the cash amount and the differential is added for card.
Set to Card, the keyed amount is the card amount and a cash discount is applied for cash.
entries.quote: it will either present as the Cash Amount (Adding the Differential) or Card Amount (Adding a Cash Discount).

entries.title: Reprint a previous batch report on the terminal
steps: Open the Reports menu.
Choose Detailed Reports.
You can reprint several previous batch reports from there.
entries.quote: You are able to Reprint previous Detailed Reports by navigating to the Reports menu followed by Detailed Reports.

entries.title: Where "Reset Terminal" (soft reset) is on each model
steps: VL100 / VL110 / VP100: Menu button, Host Utility, Reset Terminal.
VL500 / VP500: Menu button, Settings, Reset Terminal.
entries.quote: VL100/VL110/VP100 = Menu Button > Host Utility > Reset Terminal
entries.note: Routed to tech support: other Valor articles say Reset Terminal resets the terminal database.

entries.title: Level 2 / Level 3 processing
steps: Valor says L2/L3 is available on TSYS through the Virtual Terminal only, L2 is supported on physical devices, and it is not supported on First Data.
It has to be enabled on the account. Contact client services.
entries.quote: Yes, currently on TSYS via our Virtual Terminal only.

entries.title: Close an open batch from the portal (merchant accounts)
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Find the most recent transaction in the open batch, select the vertical ellipsis, then Open Batch.
Select the Action button, then Close Batch.
entries.quote: Locate the most recent transaction within the Open Batch, select the Vertical Ellipsis(⋮) followed by Open Batch.
entries.note: The article says "Only Applicable to Merchant Accounts".

entries.title: Adjust a tip from the portal (merchant accounts)
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Find the most recent transaction in the open batch, select the vertical ellipsis, then Open Batch.
Select the Action button, then Add Tip.
Change the tip amount on the transaction, then select Adjust Tip.
entries.quote: Next Adjust the Tip Amount on the designated Transaction followed by Adjust Tip.

entries.title: Tip adjust is not available on debit or EBT transactions
steps: Tips cannot be adjusted on debit or EBT transactions.
entries.quote: Tip Adjust is not available to Debit or EBT Transactions.

entries.title: Void a transaction from the portal
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Find the transaction, select the vertical ellipsis, then Void Transaction.
entries.quote: Locate the Transaction, select the Vertical Ellipsis(⋮), followed by Void Transaction.

entries.title: View a transaction receipt in the portal
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Find the transaction, select the vertical ellipsis, then View Receipt.
entries.quote: select the Vertical Ellipsis(⋮) followed by View Receipt.

entries.title: Open a support ticket from the portal
steps: Go to Tickets in the sidebar menu.
Select Create Ticket.
Choose the subject: Hardware, Transaction, Statement, Payment, Other or Sales.
Select the terminal EPI that has the issue.
Describe the issue.
Select Submit. The provider receives the request and calls back.
entries.quote: Your ISO will receive this request and respond with a call back.

entries.title: Open a support ticket about one transaction
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Find the transaction, select the vertical ellipsis, then Open Ticket.
Select the subject, describe the concern, give your best call-back number, and select Submit.
entries.quote: Locate the Transaction, select the Vertical Ellipsis(⋮), followed by Open Ticket.

entries.title: Run a batch report in the portal
steps: Go to Report in the sidebar menu.
Select Batch Report.
Select Filter and set the date range and the EPI, merchant name or store number.
Select Search.
entries.quote: Select Search to show the updated list of Batch Reports.

entries.title: Run a tip report in the portal (merchant accounts)
steps: Go to Report in the sidebar menu.
Select Tip Report.
Select Filter and set the date range and EPI.
Select Search.
entries.quote: Select Search to show the updated list of Tip Reports.

entries.title: Decline reasons shown in the portal
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu and hover over the transaction status icon.

If it says DECLINE, a reason is shown, for example Insufficient funds, Expired card, Do not honor, Invalid card number, Incorrect PIN, Pick Up Card, Duplicate transaction, Call for Authorization, Transaction not permitted-Terminal or No response from the processor host.
Other listed reasons relate to the account or terminal set-up, for example Invalid Merchant ID, EPI Not Active, Merchant Not Active and Host profile info not configured properly.
entries.quote: Hovering over a Transaction Status icon, if a DECLINE is stated below are possible Decline Errors Statuses.
entries.note: Valor's list has about 130 reasons and gives no explanation or fix for any of them.

entries.title: DECLINED: Void/Full Reversal: Settlement already occurred
steps: The void was refused because settlement has already occurred for that transaction.
entries.quote: DECLINED Void/Full Reversal: Settlement already occurred
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: Tip amount cannot be more than base amount
steps: The tip entered is larger than the sale amount.
Enter a tip that is not more than the base amount.
entries.quote: DECLINED Tip amount cannot be more than base amount
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: EPI Not Active
steps: The terminal's EPI is not active.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED EPI Not Active
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: Merchant Not Active
steps: The merchant account is not active.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED Merchant Not Active
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: Host profile info not configured properly
steps: The processor (host) set-up for this terminal is not configured properly.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED Host profile info not configured properly
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: EPI host processor info not found
steps: The processor information for this EPI was not found.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED EPI host processor info not found
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: No response from the processor host
steps: The processor host did not respond.
Try the transaction again.
If it keeps happening, contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED No response from the processor host
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: Txn is already in processing state. Pls try again later
steps: The transaction is already being processed.
Wait and try again later.
entries.quote: DECLINED Txn is already in processing state. Pls try again later
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: Duplicate transaction
steps: The transaction was flagged as a duplicate of an earlier one.
Check whether the first attempt already went through before running it again.
entries.quote: DECLINED Duplicate transaction
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: Refund limit exceeded
steps: The refund is over the refund limit set on the account.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED Refund limit exceeded
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: Original transaction not found
steps: The original transaction could not be found.
Check the transaction number or card digits you entered and try again.
entries.quote: DECLINED Original transaction not found
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: DUKPT Key Error
steps: This is an encryption key error.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED DUKPT Key Error
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: DECLINED: SERV NOT ALLOWED Contact Merchant Services Technical Support
steps: The message itself says to contact merchant services technical support.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: DECLINED SERV NOT ALLOWED Contact Merchant Services Technical Support
entries.note: Valor lists this decline reason without an explanation; the steps restate the message.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: run a transaction (new portal)
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Select the Sale, Recurring, Authorization, Refund, E-Invoice, QR, Cash or Gift Card tab.
Enter the amount.
Enter the customer details: phone number, email, card details, and an invoice number and description if needed.
Tick Line Items if you want to include inventory items; enter an item SKU to fill in its details, and select any discounts.
Confirm the customer shipping and billing details.
Select Process Payment to charge the full amount now, or Validate to schedule the transaction for later.
Check the transaction and receipt details, then select Process to finish.
entries.quote: Select Validate or Process Payment to continue the Transaction.
entries.note: The article says "Only Applicable for Merchant Accounts".

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: "Validate" makes a temporary charge
steps: Validate schedules a transaction for a later time.
A temporary charge is made to confirm the card is active.
entries.quote: Validate = To Schedule a Transaction for a Later Time (A Temporary Charge will be made to Confirm Card Activation)

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: send a sale to the physical terminal (Valor Connect)
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Tick the checkbox next to Valor Connect.
Complete the transaction details.
In the Terminal drop-down at the top right, select the terminal that shows an active Valor Connect state.
Select Process Payment. The transaction completes on the physical terminal.
entries.quote: Select the Terminal that has an Active Valor Connect state in the Terminal drop-down in the top right.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: resend an e-invoice
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Select Manage, then the E-Invoices tab.
Find the transaction, select the vertical ellipsis, then Resend E-Invoice.
entries.quote: select the Vertical Ellipsis(⋮) followed by Resend E-Invoice.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: cancel an e-invoice
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Select Manage, then the E-Invoices tab.
Find the transaction, select the vertical ellipsis, then Cancel E-Invoice.
entries.quote: select the Vertical Ellipsis(⋮) followed by Cancel E-Invoice.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: create a PayNow link
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Select E-Invoice and tick PayNow Link.
Fill in the transaction details, then select Process Payment.
entries.quote: Select E-Invoice followed by checking PayNow Link.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: generate a QR code for a customer to scan and pay
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Select the QR tab, then Generate QR.
Enter the amount, and a description if needed, then select Process.
A QR code is generated, along with a link you can copy and send to the customer.
entries.quote: This will also create a Link you may copy to send to the Customer.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: stop a recurring billing
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Select Manage, then the Recurring Billing tab.
Find the transaction, select the vertical ellipsis, then Deactivate Recurring Billing.
entries.quote: select the Vertical Ellipsis(⋮) followed by Deactivate Recurring Billing.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: edit a recurring billing
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Select Manage, then the Recurring Billing tab.
Find the transaction, select the vertical ellipsis, then Edit Payment.
Change the details, then select Update.
entries.quote: Modify Transaction details followed by Update.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: switch to a different virtual terminal
steps: Go to Virtual Terminal in the sidebar menu.
Open the drop-down at the top right that shows a Virtual Terminal EPI. It lists all active virtual terminals available to your user.
Pick one and carry on with the transaction.
entries.quote: Select the drop-down box on the top-right with a Virtual Terminal EPI to present all Active Virtual Terminals available to your User Account.

entries.title: Set up your online portal password for the first time
steps: When your account is created you receive an SMS and an email with an activation link.
Click the activation link.
Create a password with at least six characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter and one number.
Enter it in both the Password and Confirm Password fields and click Confirm.
entries.quote: Create a Password that satisfies the password policy of six characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter and one numeric digit.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: run a sale
steps: Enter the transaction amount.
Enter the phone number or email address.
Enter the credit card information. It is tokenized for future transactions.
Enter an invoice number and description if you want (optional).
Scroll down and select Process.
Confirm the details in the Summary Details window. To remove the non-cash charge, click the X and enter the password.
Select Process to finalize the transaction.
entries.quote: SALE 1. Enter the Transaction Amount. 2. Enter the Phone Number or Email Address. 3. Enter the Credit card information.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: remove the non-cash charge from a sale
steps: On the Summary Details window, click the X next to the non-cash charge.
Enter the password.
entries.quote: By clicking on the X and entering the password, you can remove the Non-Cash Charge.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: void a transaction
steps: Go to the Transactions module in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis on the transaction and select Void.
Enter a phone number or email address for the receipt (optional).
Select Proceed.
entries.quote: select Void. 3. Enter the Phone Number or Email Address for the receipt (optional).

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: refund a specific transaction
steps: Go to the Transactions module in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis on the transaction and select Issue Refund.
Confirm the amount you want to refund.
Enter a phone number or email address for the receipt (optional).
Select Proceed.
entries.quote: Conﬁrm the amount you want to refund.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: refund by entering the card (not tied to a transaction)
steps: Enter the transaction amount.
Enter the phone number or email address.
Enter the credit card information. It is tokenized for future transactions.
Enter an invoice number and description if you want (optional).
Scroll down and select Process.
Confirm the details in the Summary Details window. To remove the non-cash charge, click the X and enter the password.
Select Process to finalize the transaction.
entries.quote: REFUND 1. Enter the Transaction Amount. 2. Enter the Phone Number or Email Address. 3. Enter the Credit Card information.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: run a pre-authorization
steps: Enter the transaction amount.
Enter the phone number or email address.
Enter the credit card information. It is tokenized for future transactions.
Enter an invoice number and description if you want (optional).
Scroll down and select Process.
Confirm the details in the Summary Details window. To remove the non-cash charge, click the X and enter the password.
Select Process to finalize the transaction.
entries.quote: PREAUTH 1. Enter the Transaction Amount.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: capture a pre-authorization (Ticket)
steps: Go to the Transactions module in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis on the transaction.
Select Capture Transaction.
Confirm the details in the Summary Details window.
Select Process to finalize.
entries.quote: Select Capture Transaction.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: send an e-invoice
steps: Enter the transaction amount.
Enter the phone number or email address.
Set an expiration date.
Enter the customer name, invoice number and description (optional).
Select Send E-Invoice.
entries.quote: Description (optional) 5. Select Send E-Invoice.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: send a Pay Now link
steps: In the E-Invoice form, tick the Pay Now Link checkbox.
Select the expiration date, or set it to Never Expire.
Select Flexible if the customer should enter the amount themselves.
Scroll down and select Send Pay Now.
entries.quote: You can select Flexible to allow customers to enter the amount of their choice.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: record a cash sale
steps: Enter the transaction amount.
Enter the phone number or email address.
Enter an invoice number and description (optional).
Select Process.
entries.quote: CASH 1. Enter the Transaction Amount.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: set up recurring billing
steps: Select Subscription or Installment. A subscription bills a set amount for a set period or indefinitely. An installment bills part of a total until the total is paid.
Select the date the payment should be collected.
Select the frequency: Weekly, Bi-Weekly or Monthly.
For a subscription, enter how many weeks or months it lasts, or that it never expires. For an installment, enter the number of payments needed to pay off the total.
entries.quote: In case of Installment, enter the number of payments required for the total amount to be paid

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: add line items and discounts to a sale
steps: Tick the Line Items checkbox.
Pick a SKU from the drop-down if you have added products (My Settings > Product Settings), or type in the SKU, category, description, quantity, unit cost and tax.
Select + ADD ITEM for more lines. Use the delete icon to remove a line.
To add a discount, tick Discounts and choose one from the drop-down. If the list is empty, add one under My Settings > Discount Settings.
entries.quote: If there are no discounts in the dropdown, go to My Settings > Discount Settings to add one.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: batch out (settle)
steps: Go to the Transactions module in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis.
Select Open batch.
Select Action.
Select Batch Out.
Confirm the number of transactions and the amount.
Select Yes to settle the batch.
entries.quote: Select Yes to settle the batch.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: adjust tips
steps: Go to the Transactions module in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis.
Select Open batch.
Select Action.
Enter the tip amount on the tip lines.
Scroll up and select Adjust Tip.
Confirm the number of tip adjustments and select OK.
entries.quote: Once the tip adjustment is done, scroll up and select Adjust Tip.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: what is under Manage
steps: E-Invoices: see every e-invoice sent and its status; use the vertical ellipsis to resend or cancel one.
Recurring Billing: see every recurring bill; use the vertical ellipsis to change one.
Whitelist IP Address: create rules to always allow specific IP addresses.
API Keys: create the APP ID and API Key for an online shopping cart integration.
entries.quote: Whitelist IP Address: Merchants can create rules to always allow speciﬁc IP addresses.

entries.title: Install the ValorPay app on a phone
steps: On iPhone, open the App Store, search ValorPay and select Install.
On Android, open the Google Play Store, search ValorPay and select Install.
You can also scan Valor's QR code to go straight to the app's store page.
entries.quote: Scan QR Code to be brought to the Google Play Store to Install the ValorPay App

entries.title: ValorPay app: log in for the first time (knowledge base version)
steps: Download the ValorPay app.
Enter the email address you use for the online portal and select Submit.
A one-time passcode is sent to the mobile number on file.
Set up a 6-digit passcode for the app.
Re-enter the 6-digit passcode to confirm and sign in.
entries.quote: A One Time Passcode will be sent to the Mobile Phone Number on File.

entries.title: RCKT: pair the reader with the phone (knowledge base version)
steps: Power on the RCKT by pressing and holding the Power icon. When fully on, the screen shows three lines: mPOS, a C-ME30S-685xxx number, and the date and time.
Open the ValorPay app on the phone.
Select the banner at the bottom of the screen labeled MPOS.
Select the device whose C-ME30S-685xxx number exactly matches your reader.
Select Pair to connect the phone to the RCKT over Bluetooth.
Press the green O button at the bottom right of the RCKT to confirm pairing.
The reader then loads its EPI, AID and RKI details. When that finishes you can take payments.
entries.quote: Click the Green O button on the bottom-right of the RCKT to confirm pairing to your smartphone.
entries.note: Describes the older app layout (MPOS banner). The 06/2025 QRG describes a newer layout; see the separate entry.

entries.title: ValorPay app: menu options (knowledge base version)
steps: My Ticket: open a support ticket.
E-Invoice: create an e-invoice.
Settings: change language (English or Spanish), see the logged-in email, privacy policy, logout, upload merchant logo, notification settings.
Virtual TM: process a transaction.
Batch: view or close a batch.
entries.quote: Batch = To View or Close a Batch

entries.title: ValorPay app: run a keyed transaction (Virtual TM)
steps: Select the Menu (three lines) button, then Virtual TM.
Tap SALE to choose the transaction: Sale, Auth or Refund.
Enter the transaction amount and the customer's email address and mobile number.
Select the right arrow at the top right.
If the customer has used a card before with those details, select the card and enter the CVV. Otherwise select New Card.
For a new card, enter the card number, cardholder name, expiration date and CVV/CID, then press the right arrow.
Have the customer sign on the screen, then select the right arrow.
On the final amount confirmation screen, select Pay.
entries.quote: Request the Customer Sign on the Screen followed by selecting the Right-Arrow to continue to the Final Amount Confirmation Screen. Select Pay to Complete.

entries.title: RCKT: run a card transaction (knowledge base version)
steps: Select the MPOS banner at the bottom of the app, then select your RCKT.
Tap CREDIT to choose the form of payment: Credit, Debit or Cash.
Tap SALE to choose the transaction: Sale, Void, Auth, Ticket, Refund or Presale.
Enter the transaction amount and the customer's email address and mobile number.
Swipe, insert or tap the card on the RCKT.
On the amount confirmation screen, check the details, enter the tip amount, and select the arrow at the top right.
On the final amount confirmation screen, add a non-cash fee if applicable, then select Pay.
entries.quote: Swipe, Insert or Tap the Card using the RCKT.
entries.note: Describes the older app layout.

entries.title: ValorPay app: send an e-invoice
steps: Select the Menu button, then E-Invoice.
Fill in the amount, expiration date, customer mobile number, email address, name, invoice number and description.
Select Send E-Invoice.
entries.quote: Select Send E-Invoice to Complete.

entries.title: ValorPay app: send a QR payment
steps: Select the Menu button, then E-Invoice.
Select QR Payments.
Fill in the amount, expiration date, customer mobile number, email address, name, invoice number and description.
Select Send QR Payment.
entries.quote: Description of QR Payment Transaction Details. 4. Select Send QR Payment to Complete.

entries.title: ValorPay app: send a PayNow link
steps: Select the Menu button, then QR Payment.
Select PayNow Link.
Tick Flexible if the customer should enter the amount; tick Never Expire if the link should not expire.
Fill in the amount and expiration date if they apply, plus the customer mobile number, email address, name, label and description.
Select Send QR Payment.
entries.quote: Flexible = Transaction Amount Enterable by Customer

entries.title: ValorPay app: view batches
steps: Select the Menu button, then Batch.
Use the store icon at the top left to move between your stores.
Use the device icon at the top right to move between devices.
entries.quote: Select the Device icon in the top-right to navigate between devices.

entries.title: RCKT: run a package download (AID load)
steps: Select MPOS in the mobile app.
Select your RCKT's ID.
Select the Settings icon at the top right, next to the Bluetooth icon.
Select UPDATES, then AID LOAD.
entries.quote: Select UPDATES followed by AID LOAD.

entries.title: RCKT: run an RKI (encryption key) download
steps: Select MPOS in the mobile app.
Select your RCKT's ID.
Select the Settings icon at the top right, next to the Bluetooth icon.
Select RKI DOWNLOAD.
entries.quote: Select the Settings icon in the top right of the screen next to the Bluetooth icon. 4. Select RKI DOWNLOAD.

entries.title: RCKT: connect the reader to your smartphone (06/2025 guide)
steps: Press and hold the Power icon to turn the RCKT on.
Open the ValorPay app on your smartphone.
Select the switch icon at the top right of the screen and choose your store.
Select the RCKT device whose C-ME30S-685xxx number exactly matches your reader.
Once your endpoint identifier (EPI) has loaded, you are ready to take payments.
entries.quote: Select the switch icon at the top right of the screen and choose your store.

entries.title: RCKT: transaction types available in the ValorPay app
steps: Tap SALE on the home screen to open the drop-down.
The types are: Quick Sale, Sale, Auth, Capture Auth (Ticket), Refund, Void, Balance Enquiry, Withdraw (EBT Cash), Add Value (Gift Card) and Activate (Gift Card).
entries.quote: Tap SALE to select the Transaction Type to be processed from the dropdown menu:

entries.title: RCKT: take a card payment (06/2025 guide)
steps: Select the transaction type from the drop-down next to Sale, then enter the amount.
Select RCKT as the payment method.
Enter the customer details and select Continue.
Swipe, insert or tap the card on the RCKT.
The customer enters their PIN on the RCKT if asked.
Select or enter the tip amount, then select Pay.
"Approved" shows on both the app and the RCKT when it is done.
entries.quote: “Approved” is displayed on the ValorPay App and RCKT Mobile POS screens when done.

entries.title: RCKT / ValorPay app: payment methods you can choose
steps: After entering the amount and selecting Continue, choose a payment method: RCKT, Manual, Cash, E-Invoice, PayNow, QR Pay, EBT Food, EBT Cash or Gift Card.
entries.quote: Select a Payment Method from the options available, to execute the transaction:

entries.title: RCKT: how to tell the card was read
steps: The RCKT beeps once after a card is swiped, inserted or tapped. That means it was read correctly.
A prompt to enter the PIN then shows in both the ValorPay app and on the RCKT.
entries.quote: The RCKT Mobile POS beeps once after a payment card is swiped, inserted, or tapped, indicating it was read correctly,

entries.title: RCKT: where the customer signs
steps: If on-screen or forced signature is enabled, the customer signs on the phone in the ValorPay app during the card transaction.
entries.quote: Customer signature on the mobile device during the execution of a card transaction.

entries.title: RCKT: buttons and card slots
steps: Buttons: Power, Delete, Cancel, OK, Up and Down.
The reader has a tap area, a swipe slot, an insert (chip) slot and a charging port.
entries.quote: 1. Power 6. Up 2. Delete 7. Tap 3. Cancel 8. Swipe 4. OK 9. Charging port 5. Down 10.Insert

entries.title: RCKT (dual pricing): run a sale (06/2025 guide)
steps: Use the drop-down on the left to switch to Quick Sale.
The screen shows separate card, EBT and cash prices. Enter the transaction amount and select Process Payment.
Select the payment method.
Enter the customer mobile number and email address and select Continue.
When the app prompts, tap, swipe or insert the card on the RCKT.
The app and the RCKT show a screen to enter the PIN.
When it completes, the app shows a confirmation screen with the transaction status.
entries.quote: Enter the transaction amount and select Process Payment.

entries.title: RCKT (dual pricing): run a sale (11/2024 guide)
steps: After pairing, select the mPOS banner at the bottom of the screen.
Enter the transaction amount.
Select CARD, EBT or CASH.
Tap, insert or swipe the card. EBT cards can only be swiped.
Enter the Clerk ID, if enabled.
Select one of the tip percentages or type a custom tip. The total at the top updates.
Check the amount, tip, tax and cash discount, then select Pay.
A pop-up confirms the sale was approved.
entries.quote: After entering the transaction amount the next step is to select either “CARD,” “EBT,” or “CASH”.
entries.note: Older app layout than the 06/2025 guide.

entries.title: RCKT: EBT cards must be swiped
steps: For EBT on the RCKT you can only swipe the card. Tap and insert do not apply.
entries.quote: Also note that for EBT, you can only swipe the card.

entries.title: ValorPay app: what you need before you start
steps: Install the ValorPay app on the phone.
Have valid Valor Portal login credentials (merchant or operator account).
Enable Bluetooth and GPS (location) permissions on the phone.
Make sure the phone has a stable internet connection (Wi-Fi or mobile data).
entries.quote: Bluetooth and GPS permissions are enabled on your device.

entries.title: ValorPay app: log in and set a passcode (06/2025 guide)
steps: Open the app, enter your username and select Login with OTP.
Enter the one-time passcode sent to your registered email address and mobile number. It is valid for 120 seconds.
Create a 6-digit passcode for the app.
You are taken to the home screen.
entries.quote: Note: Generated OTP is valid for 120 seconds.

entries.title: ValorPay app: the one-time passcode (OTP) does not work
steps: The OTP is only valid for 120 seconds.
It is sent to your registered email address and mobile number.
entries.quote: Enter the OTP sent to your registered Email address and Mobile number to verify your

entries.title: ValorPay app: switch store or device
steps: Select the switch icon on the top of the home screen.
Pick the store. The list shows stores set up with a Virtual Terminal or RCKT.
Pick the device. The list shows the Virtual Terminals and RCKT devices in that store.
entries.quote: The devices section displays all Virtual terminals and RCKT devices from a selected store.

entries.title: RCKT: pair the reader in the ValorPay app (06/2025 user guide)
steps: In the app, select a RCKT device from the list of devices under your store.
A screen scans for nearby RCKT devices.
Select the RCKT device EPI from the list to pair it with the physical reader.
When pairing succeeds, the app automatically runs the AID load, parameter download and RKI download.
entries.quote: Once the pairing is successful, an automatic process will complete, including AID load, Param download, and RKI download for the RCKT.

entries.title: RCKT: the app does not find the reader when pairing
steps: Make sure Bluetooth and Location permissions are enabled on the phone. The app needs both to scan for nearby RCKT devices.
The Connected Device option in the app menu scans for and connects to a nearby RCKT.
entries.quote: Ensure that Bluetooth and Location permissions are enabled on the mobile device to proceed.

entries.title: RCKT / ValorPay app: EBT or gift card option is missing
steps: EBT Food, EBT Cash and Gift Card only appear if they were enabled for the merchant when the account was set up.
Contact tech support to have them enabled.
entries.quote: option is enabled for the merchant while onboarding

entries.title: ValorPay app: sell items from inventory
steps: Select products from your inventory in the app.
On the Cart Items page, review the items and quantities. Change a quantity or remove an item if needed.
Process the transaction through the Virtual Terminal or the RCKT.
Inventory stays in sync with the Valor Portal automatically.
entries.quote: Merchants can adjust the checkout quantity or remove items from the

entries.title: RCKT: give cash back on a sale
steps: If the cashback option is enabled, a cashback screen appears during the sale.
Enter the cashback amount and select Continue to complete the transaction.
entries.quote: Having the Cashback option enabled, the merchant can enter the desired cashback amount

entries.title: ValorPay app: menu options (06/2025 guide)
steps: Connected Device: scan for and connect to a nearby RCKT.
Tickets: create a Call Me Back ticket for a store or device.
Reports: e-invoice and batch reports.
Settings: My Profile, Device Permissions, Change Passcode, Face ID or Touch ID, Change Language.
Contact: your provider's contact details.
About: app version, Knowledge Base, privacy policy.
Logout.
entries.quote: Allow the merchant to scan and establish connection with nearby RCKT device.

entries.title: ValorPay app: change the app passcode or turn on Face ID / Touch ID
steps: Open the menu and choose Settings.
Choose Change Passcode, or Face ID or Touch ID.
entries.quote: Provides access to app settings, including My Proﬁle, Device Permissions, Change Passcode, Face

entries.title: ValorPay app: ask for a call back from support
steps: Open the menu and choose Tickets.
Create a Call Me Back ticket for the store and device concerned.
entries.quote: Provides option for the merchant to create a Call Me Back ticket for any of their registered stores and

entries.title: ValorPay app: void, refund or resend a receipt for a past transaction
steps: Open Transactions. It lists every transaction on the merchant account; filter by date, status, type or card type.
Select the vertical ellipsis next to the transaction.
Choose Void Transaction, Issue Refund, Open Ticket, Email Receipt or SMS Receipt.
entries.quote: selecting the vertical ellipsis next to a transaction entry, merchants can perform Void Transaction,

entries.title: ValorPay app: capture an authorization from the transaction details
steps: Open Transactions and select the transaction.
On the Transaction Details page you can capture the authorization, issue a refund, void, open a ticket, or send an SMS or email receipt.
entries.quote: Details page displays the information provided by the merchant or operator to execute the

entries.title: ValorPay app: tip adjust, void or close the open batch
steps: Open Open Batches. It shows the open batches for the selected store or device.
For a transaction in the open batch you can Tip Adjust, Void Transaction or Open Ticket.
You can also close the open batch manually.
entries.quote: transaction within the Open batch. In addition, merchants have the option to manually close an open

entries.title: ValorPay app: what the Dashboard shows
steps: Filter by Recent, Today, Yesterday, MTD or Last Month.
It shows total amount, transaction count, average volume, pending e-invoices, unsettled transaction count, last settled batch and pending authorizations.
entries.quote: Unsettled TXN Count, Last Settled Batch, Pending Authorizations, Stores, Users, Devices, and

entries.title: Virtual Terminal in the ValorPay app: payment types
steps: Select the Sale drop-down on the home screen.
For a Virtual Terminal the types are Quick Sale, Sale, Auth, Capture Auth, Void and Refund.
Dual pricing can be enabled for both Virtual Terminal and RCKT transactions.
entries.quote: Note: Dual Pricing can be enabled for both Virtual Terminal and RCKT device transactions.

entries.title: Run a credit sale (Paysafe guide)
steps: Enter the transaction amount and tap OK.
Confirm the amount. You can remove any non-cash charge here.
Swipe, insert or tap the card. For manual entry, type the card number.
Ask the customer to sign on the screen. Enter a tip if enabled.
Enter the customer's phone number to send an SMS receipt, or select Go Green.
Tap Print Receipt if the customer wants a paper copy.
Follow the prompts to print the customer copy.
entries.quote: Confirm the amount. You can remove any non-cash charge here.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Run a debit sale (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap Credit until it switches to Debit.
Enter the transaction amount and tap OK.
Confirm the amount.
Swipe, insert or tap the card.
Ask the customer to enter their PIN. Enter a tip if enabled.
Enter the customer's phone number for an SMS receipt, or select Go Green.
Tap Print Receipt if a paper copy is needed.
entries.quote: Tap Credit until it switches to Debit.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Void a credit transaction (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap Sale until you see Void, then tap OK.
Enter your password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your EPI number.
Choose Tran Number or Card Number.
Enter the transaction number or the last 4 digits of the card.
Select the transaction to void.
Enter the customer's phone number for an SMS receipt and select Go Green, or tap Print Receipt.
entries.quote: Tap Sale until you see Void, then tap OK.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Refund to a credit card (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap Sale until you see Refund.
Enter the transaction amount and tap OK.
Confirm the amount. Non-cash charges are not applied to refunds.
Enter your password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your EPI number.
Swipe, insert or tap the card.
Ask the customer to sign and confirm.
Choose the receipt option.
entries.quote: Confirm the amount. Non-cash charges are not applied to refunds.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Print a pre-sale ticket (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap the keypad icon, then press 2.
Enter your password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your EPI number.
Press 2 again.
Enter the amount. The ticket prints automatically.
On VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550 models instead: tap the Menu icon, tap Page Down, tap Option 2 (Host Utility), enter the password, select Pre-Sale Ticket, enter the amount and tap OK.
entries.quote: Tap the keypad icon, then press 2, enter your password, and press 2 again.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap the star icon, then tap 1, Print Receipt. The last transaction receipt prints.
Press Yes for a customer copy, or No to exit.
For older receipts, tap the keypad icon, press 4, and choose option 2 or 3.
entries.quote: For older receipts, tap the keypad icon, press 4, and choose option 2 or 3.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Settle the batch (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap the star icon, then press 2 on the keypad.
A summary report prints.
A detailed report is emailed to the address linked to your business settings. You can update the email address in the portal.
entries.quote: A detailed report will be emailed to the address linked to your business settings.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Adjust a tip (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap the star icon, then press 3.
Choose Tran Number or Card Number.
Enter the transaction number or the last 4 digits of the card.
Select the transaction to adjust.
Choose a pre-configured tip amount or enter a custom amount.
Tap OK to confirm.
Choose whether to print a merchant copy.
Select Yes to adjust another tip, or No to finish.
entries.quote: Select Yes to adjust another tip, or No to finish.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Settings changed in the portal are not showing on the terminal (Paysafe guide)
steps: Changes only take effect after a Package Download on the terminal. This also applies to general software updates.
Tap the Favorites button (the star icon at the bottom left of the screen).
Select 6, Package Download.
Tap OK.
entries.quote: After making any modifications to device parameters in the Online Portal, you must perform a Package Download on the terminal to apply these changes.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Invalid Parameter (Paysafe guide)
steps: Close the terminal's batch first (it can be closed from the online portal).
Then try the download or parameter update again.
entries.quote: If you encounter an "Invalid Parameter" error
entries.note: Paysafe notes this was documented for the VL500 and is "generally applicable to similar Valor devices".

entries.title: Software update is not reaching the terminal (Paysafe guide)
steps: App Download must be switched to Enabled for the terminal in the online portal. Tech support does this.
After the update has been pushed, the App Download toggle in Device Management shows Disabled again and the new version shows on the Device Management screen.
entries.quote: For any software updates or app downloads to properly push to the terminal, ensure that App Download is toggled to Enabled for your terminal within the Online Portal.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Change the terminal password (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap the star icon, then press 5.
Enter your current password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your EPI number.
Enter your new 4-digit password.
Re-enter it to confirm.
entries.quote: Enter your new 4-digit password.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Set a custom password (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap the Menu button (three lines), then the Down Arrow, and select Setup.
Tap Change Password, then choose which password to update.
entries.quote: Tap Change Password, then choose which password you’d like to update.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; the steps use the star-key layout of the VL100-type models and may describe a different software build.

entries.title: Find out why a transaction declined (Paysafe guide)
steps: In the online portal, open the Transactions tab and hover over the decline icon to see the detailed reason.
Common messages include "Transaction not permitted-Terminal", "Invalid transaction", "Insufficient funds" and "Expired card".
entries.quote: Common decline messages include "Transaction not permitted-Terminal," "Invalid transaction," "Insufficient funds," or "Expired card".
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article; not from Valor.

entries.title: Transaction not permitted (manual entry) (Paysafe guide)
steps: When this appears while keying a card in by hand, manual entry is probably not enabled in the terminal's configuration.
Contact tech support to have manual entry enabled for both credit and debit.
entries.quote: If you encounter a "Transaction not permitted" message, specifically when attempting a Manual Entry
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article; not from Valor.

entries.title: SERV NOT ALLOWED / Transaction not permitted-Card / Transaction restricted (Paysafe guide)
steps: The card type is not supported on the merchant account, for example an AMEX card when the account is not set up for AMEX.
The card type has to be enabled on the account. Contact tech support.
entries.quote: you might see errors like "SERV NOT ALLOWED Transaction not permitted-Card" or "Transaction restricted".
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article; not from Valor.

entries.title: V0062 (Paysafe guide)
steps: This usually means the card type being used is not authorized on the account (for example AMEX).
Check that the terminal is set up to accept that card type.
If it is not, the card type has to be enabled. Contact tech support.
entries.quote: The V0062 error usually means you're trying to process a transaction with a card type that isn’t authorized (e.g., AMEX).
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article; not from Valor. Valor's own knowledge base does not list V0062.

entries.title: Empty ID Package (Paysafe guide)
steps: This typically means a merchant file is being installed on a demo terminal, or a demo file on a merchant terminal.
The correct file type has to be loaded: merchant builds for merchant terminals, demo builds for demo terminals.
Contact tech support.
entries.quote: This error typically means a merchant file is being installed on a demo terminal (or vice versa).
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article; not from Valor. Valor's own knowledge base does not list this message.

entries.title: Connect or reconnect Wi-Fi (Paysafe guide)
steps: From the home screen, tap the Menu icon (three horizontal lines at the bottom).
Tap 7 Comm Config.
Tap Comm Config, then Wi-Fi.
Tap your network name (SSID), then Configure.
Enter the Wi-Fi password. It is case sensitive. For lowercase letters or special characters press the key several times (lowercase a is the 2 key five times; % is the # key five times).
Tap OK, press the Cancel button, then tap Connect.
entries.quote: Tap the SSID (your Wi-Fi network name), then tap Configure.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article written for the Valor VL100, VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550. Valor's own guide reaches Comm Config from the Favorites (star) menu.

entries.title: Connect by Ethernet / switch to the wired connection (Paysafe guide)
steps: Plug the Ethernet cable into the LAN port.
Valor devices fail over automatically to another available connection if the primary one fails.
If the terminal was on Wi-Fi before you plugged in Ethernet, you may need to tap the connection icon and select LAN yourself.
A wired connection is generally recommended to avoid Wi-Fi interference.
entries.quote: If you were previously on Wi-Fi and then connected via Ethernet, you might need to manually select LAN from the connection icon.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article written for the Valor VL100, VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550.

entries.title: Connection problems continue (Paysafe guide)
steps: If connectivity issues persist, reboot the device.
Paysafe says that on VL100 / VL110 / VP100 this can be done at Menu > Host Utility > Reset Terminal.
entries.quote: If connectivity issues persist, reboot the device.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article written for the Valor VL100, VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550. Conflict: Valor's knowledge base says Reset Terminal clears the terminal database and needs a master password; Valor's own Reboot is on the Favorites menu. Prefer Favorites > Reboot.

entries.title: Curl Error (Paysafe guide)
steps: Reboot the device.
Run a test transaction.

Make sure the device is connected to the internet. Ethernet: plug the cable into the LAN port underneath the device. Wi-Fi: tap the star icon, press 7 for Comm Config, press 2 for network options, select Wi-Fi, choose your SSID, enter the password and tap OK.
If it continues, run a ping test: tap the Menu icon, scroll to Utility and select it, tap Comm Config, then Config, then Ping. When it shows "Network Domain www.google.com", tap OK.
entries.quote: Curl Error Reboot the device Run a test transaction Make sure the device is connected to the internet
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article written for the Valor VL100, VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550. Valor's RMA page lists Curl Error as a cause for return when it cannot be resolved.

entries.title: Run a ping test (Paysafe guide)
steps: Tap the Menu icon (three lines).
Scroll to Utility and select it.
Tap Comm Config, then Config, then Ping.
When prompted with "Network Domain www.google.com", tap OK.
entries.quote: When prompted with “Network Domain www.google.com”, tap OK.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article written for the Valor VL100, VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550.

entries.title: Power the terminal down (Paysafe guide)
steps: Hold the Power button to power down the terminal.
entries.quote: Hold the Power button to power down the terminal.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article written for the Valor VL100, VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550.

entries.title: Let support troubleshoot remotely (Paysafe guide)
steps: Select Remote Diagnostics from the Favorites menu. It lets the provider troubleshoot the device remotely.
On VL100 models, tap the star icon and press 9 on the keypad.
entries.quote: For VL 100 models, simply tap the (★) icon and Press 9 on the keypad.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article written for the Valor VL100, VL100 Pro, VP100 and VP550.

entries.title: Charging problems or battery behaving inconsistently (Paysafe guide)
steps: Use the charging cable and wall adapter that came with the terminal. Unapproved accessories may charge inconsistently.
Fully discharge the battery: let it reach 0% and power itself off.
Then charge the terminal overnight to recalibrate the battery.
entries.quote: Using unapproved accessories may lead to inconsistent charging.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; we list the battery-powered models.

entries.title: Keep the battery above 45% for printing (Paysafe guide)
steps: For best operation, especially when printing receipts, keep the terminal at 45% battery or more.
entries.quote: For optimal operation, especially when printing receipts, ensure your terminal has at least 45% battery life.
entries.note: Processor (Paysafe) article for "Valor terminal"; we list battery models with a printer.
